subject: Migration staffing & comms playbook — API model evolution
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Migration staffing & comms playbook — API model evolution

Team — initiating a short cross-functional runbook for the upcoming model evolution (internal name: model-2027-release). Goals: minimize customer impact, clear staffing for canary waves, and a tight comms calendar. High-level asks: 
- Confirm staffing owners for Wave 1 pilot (target customers: Acme Health, BrightAI).
- Review attached migration matrix (migration-matrix-v1-v2.xlsx) for exemptions and non-compatible integrations.
- Approve customer comms draft attached (customer-comms-draft.md) or propose edits by EOD 6/10.
- Flag any SLA exception requests or customers that need dedicated capacity.

Target schedule (proposed)
- Pilot canary: start 2027-06-15 (3 customers)
- Broad migration window: 2027-07-10 -> 2027-07-20 cutover

Please reply with owner lines and any blockers. I attached a draft comms and the matrix for review.

Attachments: migration-matrix-v1-v2.xlsx, customer-comms-draft.md

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Group Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Migration staffing & comms playbook — API model evolution

Thanks Lauren — reviewed the matrix. Quick notes: 
- Capacity: For Acme Health and BrightAI I recommend reserving Dedicated slots for the pilot week (6/15-6/22) to avoid cold-start latency surprises. That will require 2 extra GPU nodes (estimating 80% buffer).
- Canary suggestion: 3-step canary (internal smoke -> 1 enterprise customer -> 2 more customers) with a 24h metric window for error/latency/regression. See attached canary-runbook.pdf.
- Staffing: I can own the runtime coordination (setup/scale) but need an infra engineer for the pilot week (propose assigning an on-call engineer from infra on 6/14-6/23).

Action items: 
1) Assign infra on-call (owner: ? ) by 6/07
2) Lauren to confirm pilot customer opt-in by 6/07
3) Stephanie to finalize customer-facing timeline copy by 6/10

Attachment: canary-runbook.pdf

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Inference Operations
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-03T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Migration staffing & comms playbook — API model evolution

Agree with Marcus — small additions from comms/product side: 
- Two-track comms: (A) Technical notice for integrators (detailed changelog + migration steps) and (B) Customer-facing note (impact + CTA to opt-in or request help).
- Comms cadence: send an early notice (6/08), technical migration guide (6/12), reminder + scheduled maintenance windows (6/30).
- Success metrics to gate rollout: <1% request error-rate delta, <10% latency regression p95, no model-behavior regressions on our smoke prompt set.

I've edited the customer-comms-draft.md with suggested language and a short FAQ. Will add an executive two-line summary after we lock dates.

— Stephanie
Director, Product Marketing
From: security-team@acmehealth.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-06-03T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Migration staffing & comms playbook — questions on residency & logs

Hi Lauren — thanks for the heads up. A couple of items our security team needs clarified before we opt-in for the pilot: 
1) Data residency: will requests routed to the new model be processed in the same region as today? We require EU-only processing for PHI-related workloads.
2) Audit logs: what retention window will be applied to request/response logs for the new model? We need 12 months of immutable audit logs for our compliance audit.
3) SOC2 evidence: can you share the latest SOC2 report and the controls that cover model serving?

Can we do a 30-min call this week if helpful — ops@acmehealth.com can coordinate times.

— Acme Security (external)
From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: security-team@acmehealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-03T16:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Migration staffing & comms playbook — questions on residency & logs

Hi — thanks for the questions, happy to clarify: 
- Data residency: Pilot routing will respect the per-account region setting. For Acme, we will pin routing to eu-west-1 for the pilot. No requests will leave the region for processing.
- Audit logs: We will enable immutable audit logs with a 12-month retention window for pilot accounts. Logs are written to customer-owned S3 buckets when configured; otherwise, we provide read-only exports for compliance.
- SOC2: attaching a redacted SOC2 summary and the control mapping for serving (see related link: https://docs.redwood.ai/roadmaps/migration-2027). Full SOC2 is available under NDA; we can portal that to your security mailbox.

Propose a 30-min sync tomorrow 6/04 10:00-10:30 UTC — please confirm.

Attachments: SOC2-summary-redacted.pdf (reference only)

— Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-04T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Migration staffing & comms playbook — rollout gating and exceptions

Folks — quick pass on gating criteria and exception handling (pulling from migration-matrix-v1-v2.xlsx):
- Gate to continue from canary -> broad: all three must be green on the metric window (error-rate, latency regression, quality eval). If any metric fails, rollback to previous model and open a postmortem.
- Exceptions: integrations that use non-standard tokenization or custom kernels will be added to an "exemption list". Exemptions require an engineering sign-off and a dedicated migration slot.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to model-compat-lite if latency spikes >50% or error-rate >2% for 10m. Ops will trigger fallback; Marcus please confirm runbook automation.

Requesting approval from Michael for SLA exceptions for the following customers: Acme Health (enterprise) — allow temporary SLA leniency for the first week of pilot. Please advise by EOD 6/06.

— Rishi
Product Ops
From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-04T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Migration staffing & comms playbook — approval and one constraint

Team — overall I approve the approach. Two quick points: 
1) Approve dedicated capacity for pilot and canary automation as proposed. Marcus, proceed with assigning infra on-call and schedule the canary-run automation.
2) Constraint: we will not grant SLA exceptions for non-enterprise customers. Acme Health approved for pilot (they're enterprise) is OK; no blanket SLA relaxations beyond that.

Please send me an exec-facing 2-line customer summary and the finalized comms by 2027-06-10 (I will need it for the customer steering committee on 6/11). Also add an item to the Redwood Console roadmap to surface per-route performance changes during the migration window.

— Michael Grant
VP, Product Strategy
